description: A music video producer must approve the final plan for a one-day rooftop performance shoot, including the playback method, performer rigging, brand treatment, and final-cut approval terms.

shared_context.S1: The production plans to film a rooftop performance video at Harbor Roof next month.
shared_context.S2: Mara makes the final call on whether the shoot plan is approved.
shared_context.S3: The current draft plan uses live amplified playback, a two-person aerial rig, a branded bar set, and ordinary editorial approval.
shared_context.S4: At the final lock meeting, production routinely gets a verbal signoff from the location, safety, and artist representatives before the producer approves the plan.

PF1.text: Leon confirmed with the city film office that Harbor Roof's permit prohibits amplified sound during filming, so the performance must use silent playback with the finished music added in post; the permit email is still in Leon's location folder awaiting the routine closeout packet.

PF2.text: Nia's roof-anchor inspection found that the certified anchor supports one performer only and requires a fall-arrest harness, with no pyrotechnics permitted on the roof; she completed the inspection this morning but has not yet entered the result in the production safety log.

PF3.text: Owen confirmed that the artist's signed rider prohibits visible alcohol branding and requires the artist to approve the final cut before release; he received the countersigned rider from the artist's lawyer yesterday but has not uploaded it to the shared production file.

acceptance_conditions: The performance must use silent playback with the music added in post, because the city permit prohibits amplified sound.
The aerial plan must use one performer with a fall-arrest harness and no pyrotechnics, because of the inspected roof anchor restrictions.
The video must contain no visible alcohol branding, as required by the signed artist rider.
The artist must receive final-cut approval before release, as required by the signed artist rider.
A permit-compliance commitment must be logged and supported by Leon's revealed permit fact.
A safety-rigging commitment must be logged and supported by Nia's revealed inspection fact.
An artist-rights commitment must be logged and supported by Owen's revealed rider fact.

decisive_facts.why: The city's amplified-sound prohibition changes the playback method from live amplified playback to silent playback with music added in post and requires a permit-related commitment.
The inspected anchor rating changes the aerial plan from a two-person rig to one performer with a fall-arrest harness and no pyrotechnics and requires a safety-related commitment.
The signed rider changes the brand treatment to remove visible alcohol branding, adds mandatory artist final-cut approval, and requires an artist-rights-related commitment.
